key_themes: Global semiconductor selloff: KOSPI fell 10%, Samsung and SK Hynix each dropped 12%+, spreading panic into U.S. chip stocks
AI valuation reckoning: prominent investors (Dan Niles) trimmed semi exposure, questioning hyperscaler ROI on AI infrastructure spend
Defensive rotation into healthcare, consumer staples, and utilities as tech names sold off sharply

stocks.reason: Fell ~13% to $1,051 as South Korea-led memory chip selloff (SK Hynix, Samsung each -12%) spilled into U.S. names ahead of Micron's June 24 earnings; BofA separately raised price target to $1,500
Dropped ~3.2% to $201.97 amid broad AI/semiconductor selloff and investor concerns about hyperscaler return on AI infrastructure spend; stalled at $200 level
Fell ~5% to $523 in Korean-led chip selloff; bulls called the drop a healthy flush of momentum speculators given AMD's 38% YoY revenue growth last quarter
Dropped ~5% to $134 in sympathy with the broad semiconductor selloff triggered by KOSPI circuit-breaker session
Tumbled ~24% after the company announced plans to raise $200 million through a registered direct offering of common stock, causing significant shareholder dilution
Fell ~5.4% after Q4 FY2026 earnings: EPS beat ($6.31 vs $5.95 est) but margins missed; company cited trade policy changes, rising costs, and muted package demand; FY end changed to Dec 31
Fell ~10% after hours in first earnings since May IPO: revenue +92% YoY to $193.4M, but 2026 sales guidance of $855-$865M disappointed investors seeking higher targets; $20B OpenAI deal disclosed
Rose ~4%, bucking the tech selloff, after JPMorgan upgraded to Overweight and raised price target to $291 from $270 on improved growth outlook
Gained ~1.7%, bucking the broader downturn, after boosting fiscal 2026 share repurchase program by $2B to more than $7.5B total — a 62% increase versus the prior year's level
Upgraded to Overweight from Neutral at Piper Sandler, which raised price target to $550 from $450, citing improving EDA software demand and AI chip design tailwinds
Upgraded to Outperform from Peer Perform at Wolfe Research with a $162 price target as analysts see a turnaround opportunity in the discount retailer
Downgraded to In Line from Outperform at Evercore ISI, which cut price target to $46 from $57, citing continued demand headwinds and limited near-term catalysts
Rose ~2% as investors rotated into defensive consumer staples names to avoid the broad technology and semiconductor rout

Upgraded to Peer Perform from Underperform at Wolfe Research, which cited Palantir's Ontology framework as a key differentiator and noted the stock is down 26% in 2026, reflecting improved risk/reward
